cue_correspondence.text: Pending calls let dispatchers prepare a record before releasing
it to selected responders.
This walkthrough uses one clearly marked software exercise
in a fictional department.

cue_correspondence.text: Enter a recognizable Name and a concise Nature, then review Priority and Type.
We select Routine and Investigation.
The location and destination remain blank in this small example; for

literal_source_labels: Save as pending (do not dispatch yet)
The call is saved and numbered, but nobody is notified and the field apps do not see it. Recipients you pick are kept as the proposed dispatch; dispatch it later from Pending Calls.

cue_correspondence.text: Turn on Save as pending, do not dispatch yet.
Read the explanation beside the switch.
The call will be saved and numbered, with any selected recipients
retained as a proposed dispatch.
Saving a pending record and dispatching it are separate decisions.
This is useful when a dispatcher needs to finish a nonurgent request or review
its recipient list before releasing it.

cue_correspondence.text: Select Closed under Close Type and enter a Close Note that
identifies the training activity.
Turn off Notify everyone on the call for this local cleanup.
Read back the type, complete note and switch before selecting
the final Close Call button.
Close only your exercise record; keep unrelated incidents and
their command boards intact.

The same prepare and review pattern can serve fire and EMS, community
care and mental health teams, search and rescue, security, wildland
contractors, and industrial teams.
This browser exercise confirms these application records; it does not establish
notification delivery, a physical response or native device behavior.
